messages:
mike (ACME): Hey team — seeing intermittent SSE streaming drops from our Dedicated cluster behind corporate proxy. Client sees partial chunks then reconnects, sometimes resumes, often duplicates tokens. started after we moved to the new edge appliance. Anyone seen similar?

sara (Support): Thanks Mike — can you paste a minimal repro (curl or browser) and last few bytes received? also which deployment: Dedicated in our eu-west-1 VPC?

mike (ACME): Yes dedicated eu-west-1, small fleet. Repro: curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxx' \
 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=redwood-small'

Client log: partial event (truncated) then connection reset: `data: {"delta":"Hel` then TLS close. Happens ~30-90s into stream for long responses.

omar (SRE): Quick Qs: 1) Do you go through a corporate HTTP proxy / appliance (BlueCo/CorpEdge)? 2) MTU on the path? 3) Any proxy response buffering or traffic inspection?

mike (ACME): Yes we have CorpEdge doing TLS terminate+inspect, they recently bumped inline inspection firmware. MTU default 1500 on their box. They have response buffering enabled (to scan).

jia (Runtime Eng): This smells like proxy-induced buffering/fragmentation. SSE relies on timely chunk boundaries. If the proxy reassembles or buffers until certain size or timeout, we can end up with truncated flushes or forced connection resets when the proxy reaches a max buffer or timeout.

ingress-proxy-bot: automated note: recent config push to corp-edge v3.14.2 on 1805100000 included http.response_buffer_limit=64KB and connection_idle_timeout=45s.

omar (SRE): Can you capture a tcpdump on the client side showing the final packets when drop happens? Interested in sequence: is FIN/RST coming from proxy or backend. Also curl with --trace may help.

mike (ACME): Attached tcpdump excerpt (hex trimmed) — see pattern: server sends chunks, last chunk partial, then probe from proxy ACKs followed by RST from proxy IP.

sara (Support): Based on the tcpdump and the bot note, likely the corp proxy enforces a 45s idle and will reset long-lived streams that appear idle while client processes tokens. Streaming SLO depends on small flushes. Do you use newline-flush in the client?

mike (ACME): client reads as data arrives. We see long pauses of 20-40s where no bytes are delivered then a burst. Proxy probably buffering until content-size threshold then flush+scan. During that buffering it may hit idle timeout and drop.

jia (Runtime Eng): Two-pronged approach: 1) short-term workaround: switch to smaller server-side flush size (send keepalive SSE comment lines) to keep the connection active. On Redwood you can enable a keepalive header in request: `X-Redwood-Stream-Keepalive: 10s` (server will emit `:keepalive\n\n` every 10s). Try that and see if proxy still considers connection idle. 2) Long-term: ask CorpEdge team to disable response buffering for this route or raise buffer limit/timeout. For nginx-like proxies, setting `X-Accel-Buffering: no` helped customers.

omar (SRE): Additional reproducible test: use socat to open raw TCP stream to edge appliance to see whether TLS termination vs raw proxy behavior differs. Also try curl with `--http1.1 --no-buffer -H 'Connection: keep-alive' -H 'X-Redwood-Stream-Keepalive: 10s' -v` — collect timing.

mike (ACME): Tried keepalive header — after enabling we saw stream alive beyond 60s consistently in 3/3 runs. Good sign. Still saw a single hit where the proxy inserted a large scan delay and then reset; corp said it performed payload inspection and temporarily locked the flow.

sara (Support): Great progress. For the one-off, can you provide corp proxy logs around the reset time? They often log `buffer_overflow` or `scan_timeout`.

mike (ACME): CorpEdge logs: `inspection_engine:scan_timeout, session_id=abc123, buffered=72KB, action=reset`. They have a hard 64KB scan buffer and 45s timeout after change.

jia (Runtime Eng): Confirmed root cause: proxy buffer + scan timeout. Recommendations: 1) Keepalive header to avoid idle timeout. 2) If possible, mark endpoint as `no-inspect` or raise buffer limit for that upstream (enterprise policy). 3) If marking not possible, switch to a non-inspected egress path for streaming traffic (dedicated proxy bypass). 4) As fallback, use polling (non-streaming) or smaller chunking from client side (request shorter max tokens).'

omar (SRE): Also filing an internal ticket to add a prominent troubleshooting note in our Dedicated/Private docs about corporate proxies and SSE: include suggested headers, curl repro, tcpdump patterns, and sample proxy configs (`X-Accel-Buffering: no`, `proxy_buffering off`, increase `proxy_read_timeout`). ticket: INF-2389.

mike (ACME): Thanks all. One last oddity — we saw duplicate tokens after reconnect (client resumed from server and got overlapping tokens). Is that expected?

jia (Runtime Eng): When client reconnects mid-stream we try to support idempotent resumes only when a resume token or offset is provided. Otherwise the server may resend last token fragment. Workaround: client should track last confirmed token and drop duplicates. We're discussing adding an explicit resume protocol for Dedicated/private to avoid duplicates. Filed RFC internal: RUNTIME-742.

sara (Support): I'll keep this thread open until corp confirms config changes. Mike — if you can, collect a final clean curl -v trace with keepalive header and attach to INF-2389. We'll coordinate with eng and your corp network team. :thumbsup:

mike (ACME): Will do, thanks everyone!
